text.p: Improved world aluminium prices would help boost Indian Aluminium Company's sales and profits in 1997/98 (April-March), vice chairman said on Monday.

"World alumina and aluminium prices are firming," said Tapan Mitra. "..Price realisations (will) improve. With expanded capacities, the company expects a substantial increase in volume in all its businesses."
He said 1996/97 profits fell sharply due to higher costs, sluggish domestic market and severe shortage of electricity.
Net profit fell to 591.9 million rupees from 1.14 billion in 1995/96, results released by the firm on Monday showed.
The firm, in which Canada's Alcan Aluminium Ltd holds 34.6 percent, plans to invest 1.7 billion rupees in 1997/98 for expansion and upgradation, Mitra told reporters.
"We need this investment not only to cut the cost but also to increase quality of production," he said.
Mitra said the expansion and upgradation programmes included modernisation of sheet rolling mills with inputs from Alcan.
He said the company's extrusion plant in India's southern state of Kerala would also be upgraded.
